newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends down, Shenzhen's up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends down, Shenzhen's up.

text.p: The Shanghai B share index ended slightly down on Thursday with a wary mood prevailing due to concerns about a possible new crackdown on market volatility, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index edged down 0.225 points or 0.31 percent to 73.102 on volume of 21.6 million shares worth $12.1 million.

But Shenzhen's B shares ended firmer after the Shenzhen-based Securities Times reported the city planned to set up a new stock data network in Hong Kong and encourage more B share firms to obtain secondary listings on overseas bourses.
The Shenzhen B share index rose 0.91 points or 0.58 percent to 158.67 on turnover of HK$64.56 million.
"The news has injected fresh confidence into the market because it shows Shenzhen is taking care of its market," an analyst with J & A Securities said.
Of the 44 B share companies listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, only China Merchants Shekou Port Service Holdings Co Ltd currently has a secondary listing abroad, in Singapore.
Livzon Pharmaceutical was the best performer in Shenzhen, up HK$0.24 or 4.63 percent to HK$5.42 on volume of 108,100 shares.
On the Shanghai market, brokers said domestic unwinding selling emerged amongst B shares later in the session in line with falls on the A share market, which pushed the index down.
"But the downward potential is limited because B shares have not risen as sharply as A shares over the past few weeks," one broker said.
Shanghai Lianhua Fibre was the biggest loser on profit-taking, slipping $0.020 or 9.52 percent to $0.190 on volume of 48,000 shares.

Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products traded the most with institutional investors' mixed over its annual report published on Thursday, falling $0.004 or 0.52 percent to $0.754 on volume of 3.5 million shares.
The Shanghai A share index erased its morning gains in the afternoon session on investor jitters over a possible crackdown, brokers said.
The A index fell 5.225 points or 0.39 percent to 1,344.302 on heavy turnover of 12.98 billion yuan. The SSE30 index fell 24.318 points or 0.68 percent to 3,536.098 points.
Xinjiang Zhonghe was the biggest loser on lower-than-expected earnings, plunging 1.80 yuan or 10.00 percent to 16.20 yuan on volume of 548,100 shares.
The Shenzhen A index slipped 4.15 points or 0.89 percent to end at 461.52 on turnover of 10.67 billion yuan.
